world.h: Saudi, Pakistani, Turkish officials due in Tehran
world.b: Al Jazeera's live coverage: Saudi, Pakistani and Turkish defence officials are due in Tehran for security talks with Iran.
world.title: Iran to hold security talks with Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan

national.h: U.S. measles cases top double last year's total
national.b: CDC data show more than 4,580 measles cases nationwide this year, more than double the total for all of 2025. Ninety-six percent of those infected were unvaccinated or of unknown status.
national.title: U.S. measles cases more than double what they were last year as outbreak spreads

national.h: Texas cop's ICE work tore his town apart
national.b: ProPublica profiles Jaron Alexander of Ingram, Texas, one of more than 29,000 local officers on the front lines of the Trump administration's deportation campaign.
national.title: The Small-Town Cop Who Helped ICE Deport His Neighbors

politics.h: Appeals court sceptical of Trump's California suit
politics.b: A Trump-appointed judge on a three-judge panel voiced doubt that the administration's lawsuit over California voter rolls would hold up, citing the Constitution's Elections Clause after a rare weekend argument.
politics.title: US appeals court sceptical of Trump’s lawsuit over California voter rolls

politics.h: Judge asked to force release of Kennedy Center texts
politics.b: Lawyers for Rep. Joyce Beatty are seeking a court order for the administration to turn over emails and texts about Kennedy Center plans that it has withheld as privileged presidential communications.
politics.title: Judge asked to compel Trump administration to disclose emails and texts about Kennedy Center plans

politics.h: Peltola and family hurt in minor car crash
politics.b: Another vehicle crashed into the one carrying Alaska Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola and her family on the way to the Alaska Federation of Natives banquet; they suffered minor injuries, the campaign said.
politics.title: Alaska Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola and her family suffer minor injuries in car crash

politics.h: Trump escalates attacks on El-Sayed in Michigan
politics.b: At a Port Huron rally, Trump again attacked Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed's faith. El-Sayed, a former public health official, has repeatedly said he is loyal to the U.S. and disavowed the Muslim Brotherhood.
politics.title: Trump escalates rhetoric against El-Sayed as he tries to undermine Democrat in Michigan Senate race

politics.h: Blanche defends DOJ suit over Alaska Senate race
politics.b: Pressed on CNN, Blanche denied that the Justice Department's lawsuit to stop Alaska from automatically certifying its Senate result if the Republican incumbent loses is setting the stage for Trump to challenge the midterms.

international.h: US says it helped move 1.5 billion barrels via Hormuz
international.b: The US military said more than 3,000 commercial vessels transited the Strait of Hormuz with its support over six months, helping Gulf states export 1.5 billion barrels of oil despite Iranian threats.

international.h: China's Communist Party elite open plenum
international.b: Roughly 300 Central Committee members began a closed-door plenum Monday as Xi Jinping pushes for greater loyalty from officials, about a year before he is widely expected to secure a fourth term as party leader.
international.title: China’s political elite gather for talks on Communist Party discipline

international.h: Thousands protest Czech public media funding bill
international.b: Protesters in Prague demanded the withdrawal of legislation to abolish household licence fees for public radio and television and fund them from the state budget instead, after the lower house fast-tracked the bill in an overnight vote.

international.h: Le Pen launches campaign vowing French 'renaissance'
international.b: Marine Le Pen launched her presidential campaign before thousands of supporters in Orleans on Sunday, against a backdrop of mass demonstrations and widespread social and economic discontent.

international.h: Bulgaria's presidential race heads to runoff
international.b: Record low turnout sent the race to a runoff between incumbent leftist President Iliana Yotova and Andrey Gyurov, candidate of the pro-Western reformist opposition.
international.title: Presidential race in Bulgaria heads to runoff due to record low turnout

international.h: Uganda orders Ebola quarantine for DR Congo returnees
international.b: Health Minister Chris Baryomunsi announced a 21-day quarantine for citizens returning from DR Congo, as Ebola cases in Kenya and Nigeria raise questions about travellers. Uganda says it has no active infections.

international.h: Israeli attacks kill eight in Gaza, hit university
international.b: At least eight Palestinians were killed across Gaza on Sunday, including three security guards in an Israeli air strike on the Islamic University campus in Gaza City, the second attack on the institution within a few hours.

international.h: Machado returns to Venezuela after exile
international.b: Opposition leader María Corina Machado returned to Venezuela after months in exile, writing 'I am here. With you.' Edmundo González said he would join her soon.

international.h: Burnham open to EU freedom of movement talks
international.b: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham told The Sunday Times he wants to discuss a return to EU freedom of movement as he rethinks ties with Brussels.

international.h: Lula wins Brazil run-off, holding off far right
international.b: Brazil's Superior Electoral Court called the presidential run-off for Lula, who won more than 51 percent of the vote to Flávio Bolsonaro's 48 percent, a margin of more than 4 million votes.

international.h: Algeria's senate approves troops for Niger
international.b: Algeria's upper house approved a troop deployment to Niger in an emergency session. If the lower house agrees, it would be Algeria's first mission abroad since 1973.

international.h: Israeli troops turn Hebron homes into posts
international.b: Israeli forces took over homes in southern Hebron as barracks and observation posts amid a lockdown and hundreds of raids since Friday's attack, Wafa reported.

international.h: Jordan arrests three suspects in church attack
international.b: Security forces arrested three suspects in the deadly attack on a church in Karak after they were found hiding in an abandoned house and refused to surrender, wounding them in a firefight, Jordan's Public Security Directorate said.
international.title: Jordan arrests three suspects in deadly church attack

international.h: Serbia's Vucic concedes defeat to student movement
international.b: Aleksandar Vucic, who led Serbia with virtually absolute power for 14 years, conceded defeat Sunday in an election against a diverse student-led opposition movement that spent two years protesting his government.
international.title: Serbia’s strongman leader Vucic concedes defeat to student-led movement in seismic political shift

international.h: Police clear Lisbon housing protest camp, arrest 25
international.b: Portuguese police moved in on the camp in Rossio Square early Sunday, where protesters had pitched more than 100 tents, arresting 25.

business.h: Home sellers cut prices in a stagnant market
business.b: Sellers who can are pulling listings, while others are lowering asking prices and paying thousands toward buyers' costs as surging mortgage rates stall the housing market, real estate agents say.
business.title: Home sellers are lowering their prices and helping buyers to make a deal in a stagnant market

sports.h: Thunder's Jalen Williams leaves on stretcher
sports.b: Williams suffered a gruesome lower left leg injury late in Oklahoma City's win over the Clippers. Coach Mark Daigneault said the team had no immediate update on his status.
sports.title: Thunder star Jalen Williams leaves on stretcher after gruesome leg injury vs. Clippers

sports.h: Watson's late drive keeps Browns in first place
sports.b: Deshaun Watson engineered another fourth-quarter game-winning drive in Cleveland's 27-24 win over Tennessee, his fifth this season, as the Browns sit in first place in their division.
sports.title: NFL Week 7 grades: Falcons earn solid 'A' mark, while Panthers flop with a resounding 'F'

sports.b: J.J. McCarthy impressed in his first start for New York after his trade from the Vikings, and Cam Skattebo responded emphatically to his Week 6 benching as John Harbaugh's Giants keep rolling.

sports.h: Only three undefeated FBS teams remain
sports.b: Miami, Utah and UCLA are the last unbeaten teams in FBS, a historic low. The last time major college football had only three undefeated teams through Oct. 24 was in 1977.
Baylor fired Dave Aranda, who won the 2021 Big 12 title but posted four losing records in six full seasons.

sports.h: Brewers rally past Rays 5-4 in World Series
sports.b: The Rays scored four runs in the first inning, but Milwaukee chipped away and took the lead in the bottom of the seventh. The Brewers are 9-1 this postseason.

sports.h: Upsets throw Big 12 playoff picture into chaos
sports.b: Cincinnati snapped Texas Tech's nine-game Big 12 winning streak and Scott Frost's Knights held off BYU, a week after the Cougars rose to No. 2.

sports.h: NC State fires coach Dave Doeren
sports.b: NC State fired Dave Doeren in his 14th season after a loss to Stanford dropped the Wolfpack to 3-4.

sports.h: WNBA Finals Game 6 venue up in the air
sports.b: Game 6 of the Dream-Valkyries Finals is listed as TBD because the Hawks are scheduled to host the Cavaliers at State Farm Arena the same night.

sports.h: Petr Yan outduels Dvalishvili to keep UFC title
sports.b: Petr Yan retained his bantamweight title against Merab Dvalishvili at UFC 333 in a Fight of the Year contender.
Milwaukee beat the Rays 3-2 in Game 1 at American Family Field after a week off. Christian Yelich tripled home Jackson Chourio in a two-run first inning.

local.h: State urges New Yorkers to protect bats
local.b: With Bat Week under way, New York officials are urging outdoor adventurers to stay out of caves and mines this winter to avoid waking hibernating bats so they survive to spring.
local.title: Why New Yorkers should care about bats beyond spooky season

local.h: Serbians wait hours to vote at NYC consulate
local.b: Serbian immigrants from across the Northeast lined up down West 45th Street on Sunday to vote at the consulate near Bryant Park in the Balkan nation's parliamentary election.
local.title: Serbians forced to wait hours to vote at NYC consulate as Balkan nation holds election

local.h: Ex-NYPD detective in GWB killing out on bail
local.b: Victor Romero, 62, charged with manslaughter in the shooting death of ConEd worker Koran Irvine on the George Washington Bridge, posted $1 million bail.
local.title: Retired NYPD detective charged in George Washington Bridge killing out on $1M bail

local.h: Rural hospital cuts become NY governor race issue
local.b: Candidates for governor are trading blame as rural hospitals face cuts, including Albany Med's plan to curtail services at Columbia Memorial Health in Hudson.
local.title: Cuts to rural healthcare become key issue for upstate votes in race for NY governor

local.h: NY Archdiocese agrees to pay $800M to abuse survivors
local.b: The Archdiocese of New York agreed to pay $800 million to 1,300 people who say they were sexually abused by clergy, lay leaders and teachers. The deal is set to be signed the first week of November.

periods.name: Monday
periods.text: Sunny, with a high near 69. West wind 7 to 9 mph.

periods.name: Monday Night
periods.text: Mostly clear, with a low around 51. West wind 8 to 10 mph becoming north after midnight.

periods.name: Tuesday
periods.text: Sunny, with a high near 62. North wind 7 to 13 mph.

periods.name: Tuesday Night
periods.text: Mostly clear, with a low around 47. Northeast wind around 7 mph.

periods.name: Wednesday Night
periods.text: Partly cloudy, with a low around 53.

localgood.b: Suicide deaths in New York City fell from a peak of 601 in 2022 to 535 in 2024, health department data shows, though inequities persist across groups.
localgood.title: Suicides decline in NYC, but inequities persist across groups
